title: Platform dependence: `java.lang.Math` intrinsics, the NaN sign, the JVM locale
verdict: last bits of `sqrt`… `atan2` may vary; created NaN negative on x86-64; probes on Linux x86-64, Java 21
description: The probes ran on Linux x86-64 with OpenJDK 21.0.12. `exp`, the logarithms and `power` use `StrictMath` (fdlibm), the same on every JVM and CPU; the trigonometric functions, `cbrt` and the hyperbolic ones use `java.lang.Math`, which a JVM may compute with CPU intrinsics within 1 ulp, so their last bit may differ between x86-64 and aarch64 or between JVMs (spark-elem-rounding). A NaN created by arithmetic has the sign bit set on x86-64 and clear on aarch64 (spark-nan-sign). `upper` and `lower` follow the JVM's default locale (spark-case). Integer and decimal arithmetic, casts and `round` are the same everywhere. A double's text depends on the JVM: `Double.toString` gives the shortest digits that round-trip since JDK 19 and sometimes longer ones before. Spark turns a double into a DECIMAL through that text, so a `POWER` result stored in a `DECIMAL(38,10)` is 107511333880051872 on older JVMs and 107511333880051870 on JDK 21, and postgreSQL/numeric.sql keeps a second golden file for JDK 21.
reference: The reference treats the elementary functions as black boxes with stated laws, so a last-bit difference is allowed; it has one NaN.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.

evidence.note: the JDK 21 golden file: the same row is 107511333880051870.0000000000; the two files differ only in this line
a double cast to DECIMAL goes through `Decimal(d)`
`Decimal(value: Double)` converts the double with Scala's `BigDecimal(d)`, which reads `Double.toString`
the codegen path uses `scala.math.BigDecimal.valueOf((double) c)`, the same text

notes: `python -m sverify_dev.spark_fuzz --rows 300 --seed 738`: random rows leaning on the fact's edges, each construct run with spark.sql.ansi.enabled on and off, on the folded and the codegen path, and compared with a model of this fact (value, result type, error class). 16800 of 16800 results as the fact says; Spark's value differs from Rel.eval's (sverify's lift, reference profile) on 92 of 1500 rows compared.
It exercises the last bits of the Math and StrictMath functions against the C library's, and the sign of a created NaN, on Linux x86-64.

elem_rounding[0]: 300 rows, `exp(x)`, `sqrt(x)`, `sin(x)`, `cos(x)`, `tan(x)`, `atan(x)`, `cbrt(x)`, 8400 of 8400 results as the fact says; Spark differs from Rel.eval on 92 of 1500; elem_rounding[1]: 300 rows, `ln(x)`, `log10(x)`, `log2(x)`, 3600 of 3600 results as the fact says; nan_sign[0]: 300 rows, `-a`, `abs(a)`, `a * -1.0D`, `b - b`, 4800 of 4800 results as the fact says.
Spark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.12.1, Linux amd64, local[2], session time zone UTC.
